answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-backed vouching on a trust graph. Each agent is a vertex that posts collateral and needs two vouches from already-staked peers; if a newcomer is proven a duplicate, its vouchers are slashed too. A fake identity thus needs its own bond plus fresh, unrelated backers, so each cloned thread of trust costs more than the last, while colluding sponsors lose their stake together. Over a long slashing horizon, an established agent's locked record makes buying a duplicate dearer than earning trust openly.
